headline: Khulna: Mother confesses to killing daughter, 10th grader
summary: Seema Akter admitted her involvement in the murder of 17-year-old Arfan Hossain Nirjana before a magistrate; her husband has also been detained.
details: A mother in Khulna has confessed to killing her 17-year-old daughter, Arfan Hossain Nirjana, a class 10 student of Government Iqbal Nagar Secondary School.
Khulna Metropolitan Magistrate Ibrahim Khalil Muhim recorded the confessional statement of the mother, Seema Akter, on Friday evening, after which she was sent to jail.
The victim's father, Md Alim Hossain, has also been taken into police custody for questioning in connection with the murder.
Nirjana's body was found stuffed inside a plastic sack in front of a seven-storey building in the Prantika Residential Area under Nirala in Khulna Sadar on Wednesday night.
Initially, the family claimed the girl, who had married on April 21 this year, might have been killed by her husband.
However, police investigation, including CCTV footage and forensic evidence, led to the focus shifting toward the parents.
Investigators believe the victim was killed elsewhere before her body was packed into a sack and dumped in the residential area.
Police are continuing their investigation to uncover the full circumstances surrounding the crime.
caption:
A mother confesses to killing her own 17-year-old daughter in Khulna.

A mother in Khulna has confessed to killing her 17-year-old daughter, Arfan Hossain Nirjana, a class 10 student of Government Iqbal Nagar Secondary School.

Khulna Metropolitan Magistrate Ibrahim Khalil Muhim recorded the confessional statement of the mother, Seema Akter, on Friday evening, after which she was sent to jail.

The victim's father, Md Alim Hossain, has also been taken into police custody for questioning in connection with the murder.

Nirjana's body was found stuffed inside a plastic sack in front of a seven-storey building in the Prantika Residential Area under Nirala in Khulna Sadar on Wednesday night.

Initially, the family claimed the girl, who had married on April 21 this year, might have been killed by her husband.

However, police investigation, including CCTV footage and forensic evidence, led to the focus shifting toward the parents.

Investigators believe the victim was killed elsewhere before her body was packed into a sack and dumped in the residential area.

Police are continuing their investigation to uncover the full circumstances surrounding the crime.

headline_marked: BNP MP's [[vehicles vandalised after activists' dispute]] in Jamalpur
headline: BNP MP's vehicles vandalised after activists' dispute in Jamalpur
summary: Two cars used by a Jamalpur-2 BNP MP and a local party leader were damaged by party activists following an argument over dominance.
details: Two vehicles used by the president and general secretary of Jamalpur’s Islampur upazila BNP unit were vandalised on Friday evening following a dispute between two groups of party activists.
The incident took place around 7:30pm at the Dakbangla premises in the Islampur upazila. No injuries were reported during the clash.
The altercation stemmed from a reception programme for Sultan Mahmud Babu, lawmaker from Jamalpur-2 and president of the upazila BNP.
An argument broke out between several party leaders, including the joint general secretary of the municipal BNP and the joint general secretary of the upazila Jatiyatabadi Swechchhasebak Dal.
The dispute escalated when a group of activists, allegedly led by Hasmat and Hasan, targeted the vehicles of MP Sultan Mahmud Babu and upazila BNP General Secretary Nurul Islam Nabab.
General Secretary Nurul Islam Nabab stated that the vehicles were parked at the Dakbangla premises when they were attacked. He added that they will act according to the party's decision.
Islampur Police Station Officer-in-Charge Mizanur Rahman confirmed that police brought the situation under control and the damaged vehicles are currently in police custody.
Police stated that legal action will be taken if a formal complaint is filed.
caption:
Internal party dispute leads to the vandalism of a BNP MP's vehicle in Jamalpur.

Two vehicles used by the president and general secretary of Jamalpur’s Islampur upazila BNP unit were vandalised on Friday evening following a dispute between two groups of party activists.

The incident took place around 7:30pm at the Dakbangla premises in the Islampur upazila. No injuries were reported during the clash.

The altercation stemmed from a reception programme for Sultan Mahmud Babu, lawmaker from Jamalpur-2 and president of the upazila BNP.

An argument broke out between several party leaders, including the joint general secretary of the municipal BNP and the joint general secretary of the upazila Jatiyatabadi Swechchhasebak Dal.

The dispute escalated when a group of activists, allegedly led by Hasmat and Hasan, targeted the vehicles of MP Sultan Mahmud Babu and upazila BNP General Secretary Nurul Islam Nabab.

General Secretary Nurul Islam Nabab stated that the vehicles were parked at the Dakbangla premises when they were attacked. He added that they will act according to the party's decision.

Islampur Police Station Officer-in-Charge Mizanur Rahman confirmed that police brought the situation under control and the damaged vehicles are currently in police custody.

Police stated that legal action will be taken if a formal complaint is filed.
